Future work could extend LELA to end-to-end entity linking, where mentions have to be detected as well. Being LLM-based and model-agnostic, LELA directly benefits from evolving model capabilities, but also inherits their limitations. In particular, the generation of reasoning tokens makes LELA slower than specialized entity linking models and thus more suitable for offline processing. Additionally, LELA inherits LLMs’ limited interpretability. While our evaluation spans a broad range of benchmarks, it cannot cover every possible knowledge base or domain. Although context-based reasoning improves generalization, further research is required to assess LELA’s performance across additional settings. In particular, our evaluation focuses on English benchmarks, and evaluating LELA in multilingual or low-resource settings remains an important direction for future work.
